title: Opening a Real Port: The Twenty Lines That Decide Everything

questions.question: A port is opened with nothing but O_RDWR and a device sends a four byte payload. Measured, what arrives?
options: Nothing at all, since the port was not configured
The first byte only, because the length field is 0x04 and four is the end of file character
All of it, since the port has not been told to change anything
All of it, but slowly
questions.explanation: The message that fails is decided by how long it is, and nothing in the sending code mentions its length. Three is Ctrl-C, seventeen is XON, nineteen is XOFF, which is why this presents as a device that works except sometimes.

questions.question: What does cfmakeraw actually turn off?
options: Line buffering, echo, carriage return rewriting, flow control characters and the signal characters, all of which exist for text typed by a person
Only the echo
Hardware flow control
The baud rate conversion
questions.explanation: A terminal exists to carry text a person is editing. Every one of those behaviours destroys binary data, and which data it destroys depends on the byte values a message happens to contain.

questions.question: Why open with O_NOCTTY and O_NONBLOCK?
options: They make reads faster
Each prevents a hang: the first stops a byte from the device signalling your process, the second stops the open waiting for a carrier that will never come
Both are needed for binary data
They are required by POSIX
questions.explanation: Without O_NOCTTY a Ctrl-C byte arriving on the wire can stop your program. Without O_NONBLOCK the open waits for a modem signal a microcontroller does not assert.

questions.question: tcsetattr returned zero. What have you been told?
options: That the device accepted the baud rate
That every setting was applied
That the port is now in raw mode
That it applied at least one of the settings, not that it applied the one you cared about
questions.explanation: A rate the hardware cannot do is not an error, it is a different rate applied silently, and the symptom is a link where every frame fails its checksum. Read the settings back and check the ones that matter.

questions.question: VMIN is set to one and VTIME to zero. What happens on a link whose device has stopped talking?
options: Nothing changes, VMIN only affects the buffer size
The read returns zero after a short delay
The read waits for a byte that is not coming, and the control loop waits with it
The read returns an error
questions.explanation: Zero and zero is the only combination that returns whatever is there this instant, including nothing. Any other row of that table lets a silent device hold a loop that has a deadline.

questions.question: This lesson's Windows implementation is compiled on every build and its error paths are run, but no port is opened. Why is that stated rather than glossed over?
options: Because the code is known to be wrong
Because Windows serial ports are unreliable
A silent gap in what is tested is worse than a stated one, because a reader assumes coverage that does not exist
Because the tests would be too slow
questions.explanation: A virtual COM port needs a driver that continuous integration cannot install. A USB serial adapter with its TX wired to its RX closes the gap for about ten dollars, and until somebody does that the limit belongs written down.
